ports.note: A RATE in, not a table of numbers. The port type is `table` because that is what `rate` emits, but the value carries the RateResult with it, and only that declares what the numbers are per. A plain table connected here is refused by name rather than divided: dividing a per-house rate by a per-person one is arithmetic on two different quantities. From 0.3.0 it also takes an OPTIONAL declared study design. A rate ratio is a comparison, and what a comparison may be read as depends on the design that produced it: on South London's Table IX the company is known PER HOUSE, which is a retrospective cohort, while the sibling workflow attributes a company per sub-district and is ecological. Optional, so every existing workflow runs unchanged; nothing is refused on it in this version.

ontology.note: The receipt carries both counts, both denominators, the denominator unit, the interval bounds, the level and the method by name, so a reader is never left guessing which interval they are looking at. No SHACL shape yet. There is deliberately no multiplier property: a rate ratio is dimensionless and there is nowhere to write one.

changes.description: Machine the equation into a Methods note. Every run of this widget now writes a note to the Notes tab under Methods, carrying each computation twice -- once as the formula and once with this run's numbers substituted into it -- as LaTeX the browser typesets to MathML. The claim this answers is experiment 141's, made on 2026-10-26 and unbuilt until now: "all of our computations have equations, and these can be automatically constructed in LaTeX for automatic rendering as notes". Experiment 151 built the renderer four days later and recorded that the first machined equation was still unwritten, which is what made the 212KB converter correct rather than earned. Both forms are carried because a symbolic formula restates a textbook and the instantiated one lets a reader check the arithmetic without rerunning anything. Nothing about the arithmetic changed: the formulas were read off this widget's own implementation, which is why they state what it computes and not what a source paper states -- the computations audit that would establish the second is recorded in TODO.md and does not exist. Each interval method is cited from a source that was looked up, or the note says no source has been read for it. The two outcomes are printed rather than one being an absence, for the reason `epiInfoLabelSource` exists: a missing reference reads as nothing to say when it means nobody has looked it up. No source is cited here: a log-normal interval on a ratio of two rates is a standard construction that the implementations consulted state without attributing, so the note names none rather than naming a plausible textbook.

An optional `design` input, so a declared study design can reach the comparison it governs. The rate ratio's stated sentence then carries the design and the unit of analysis. Nothing is gated yet; gating is step 3 of the sequence in docs/directions.json. Experiment 154.

evidence.note: Checked against the real transcription and the real boundaries of Snow's South London rather than a fixture: 23 of 32 sub-districts match on the published strings and 32 of 32 after folding punctuation and spacing, and no two names collapse together. Unit checks cover each of the four reported conditions, including two parts of one name both taking a rate. Equality after normalisation is string comparison; nothing here establishes that the normalisation generalises beyond a pair of files whose nine differences are all punctuation, nor that a choropleth of the joined values is a sound reading of them. The equation note added in 0.2.0 is covered by tests/equations.test.mjs (13 unit checks, including that a method reference either renders completely or is null, that no note carries a table or a heading, and that a column name with an underscore is escaped rather than read as a subscript) and by tests/equation-notes.browser.mjs over the South London example on Chromium and WebKit, which is where it is established that the LaTeX is typeset to MathML rather than shown as its source. Both suites were mutation-checked by removing the behaviour and confirming they fail.
